questions.explanation: In both, absence from a record tells little because the observation needed for an entry was not being made.

questions.stem:
At a riverside activity centre, a group can hire kayaks to cross the river or it can use a small launch. The launch leaves only when a qualified driver is present, and no such driver is available today. The kayaks are the only other authorised way to cross from the centre. Since the group has to reach the island this afternoon, it must hire the kayaks. This is not a claim that kayaks are normally quicker or more convenient than the launch; it depends on which methods are actually available.

Which of the following most closely parallels the reasoning used in the above argument?

options.A: A gardener prefers a spade to a fork and therefore uses the spade although both are at hand.
options.B: An office has two printers. The faster one is broken, so the slower one must also be unreliable.
options.C: Three routes lead to a hall; one is closed, so the shortest of the other two is open.
options.D: A courier must deliver a parcel today. The only routes are through a tunnel or over a pass. The pass is closed, so the courier must use the tunnel.
options.E: A boat needs a permit to operate; the permit is missing, so someone should apply for one.

questions.explanation: With an exhaustive choice of two ways to meet a required goal, ruling out one forces the other. The courier faces the same structure.

questions.stem:
A company chooses materials for a street lamp on the basis of strength and cost alone. Its proposed bracket uses a rather expensive metal. A second metal will bear at least as much weight in exactly the same bracket design and costs less to buy and work. No other design choice or maintenance cost will change. The engineer therefore recommends the second metal. The recommendation does not require her to show that it is the strongest metal available, only that the original proposal has no advantage on either of the two relevant measures.

Which of the following most closely parallels the reasoning used in the above argument?

options.A: A designer chooses a bright fabric because it is both more expensive and easier to see.
options.B: A traveller accepts a slower train because it costs less, though both speed and price matter.
options.C: A baker chooses a flour because the two bags cost the same, without checking how well either works.
options.D: A builder buys the strongest material on sale without considering price.
options.E: A club cares only about price and warmth when buying coats. A cheaper coat is at least as warm as the proposed one, so the club should choose the cheaper of the two.

questions.explanation: The preferred alternative is strictly better on cost and no worse on the other criterion. Unlike the slower-train example, no trade-off is required.

questions.stem:
A garden trust promised both founder families that their names would appear on a plaque if the orchard opened. It also promised that a family would be listed only if it consented. The orchard has opened, but one family has expressly refused consent. Both promises cannot now be fulfilled literally: listing that family would break the consent promise, while omitting it would break the promise made about listing. The trust may have other reasons for preferring one promise over the other, but that would not remove the conflict it has created.

Which of the following most closely parallels the reasoning used in the above argument?

options.A: A club promises to admit everyone who applies by Friday; nobody applies until Saturday, so it admits nobody.
options.B: A library promises to lend books if requested and to send notices if they are late, but none are overdue.
options.C: A team says it will travel if the game goes ahead, then keeps its word even though some players complain.
options.D: A commemorative book promises to print each entrant's address if the book appears and never to print one without permission. It appears and an entrant refuses, so either printing or omitting that address breaks a promise.
options.E: A committee promises to hear interviews on time or pay travel costs; after a delay it pays the costs.

questions.explanation: An actual event triggers the obligation to include everyone; refusal triggers the obligation to exclude one. The book example recreates the resulting conflict.

questions.stem:
A museum analyst says every bowl decorated in the workshop of Fenn has a narrow groove just inside the foot. A collector's bowl has no groove, so the analyst rules out Fenn's workshop. A booklet says that every bowl decorated by Vale also has the groove. If the booklet is right, the same feature rules out both named workshops. Rejecting the first attribution is therefore not enough to justify the collector's proposal that the bowl came from Vale. It may have been decorated by some other workshop that has not yet been identified.

Which of the following most closely parallels the reasoning used in the above argument?

options.A: Two bands use the same emblem. A poster bears it, so the older band must have advertised the concert.
options.B: Two drivers deny breaking a rule, so exactly one of them must be telling the truth.
options.C: Two publishers always watermark their own proofs. A proof with no watermark cannot be from either if both rules hold; rejecting one publisher is no reason to select the other.
options.D: All late orders have a yellow label. This order has a yellow label, so it arrived late.
options.E: The two shops named on a receipt are both closed now, so neither existed when it was printed.

questions.explanation: A shared necessary feature is missing, so both tested sources can be excluded. The reasoning does not assume the named sources exhaust the possibilities.

questions.stem:
The port engineer has enough money to clear one of two channels and wants to maximise the number of tidal hours in which freight boats can reach the port. The two channels serve the same boats at the same hours when both are open. At other hours, only the eastern channel could carry them if cleared: its deeper approaches remain navigable when the western approaches do not. There is no hour at which clearing the west would help and clearing the east would not. On that criterion, clearing the eastern channel is the better choice.

Which of the following most closely parallels the reasoning used in the above argument?

options.A: Two contractors cover different streets, and one costs less, so price settles which will cover more streets.
options.B: Two crews are available for the same shifts, but one is quicker, so it must be available for more shifts.
options.C: Two rooms would serve the same exam sessions at common opening times. One is also available for extra sessions and never loses a session the other could serve, so it is better for maximising sessions.
options.D: Two routes share most of their stops, so neither can provide access to any place the other misses.
options.E: Two wireless networks cover different rooms, with some overlap, so the network with fewer overlapping rooms must cover more rooms altogether.

questions.explanation: The eastern channel serves a strict superset of the hours served by the western one. The exam-room option uses the same inclusion argument.

questions.stem:
At a public swimming pool, children can enter the deep lane without an adult only after demonstrating that they can swim its full length. The lane is particularly deep at both ends, and a child unable to finish the length would not have a shallow place to stand. Some children are disappointed when staff refuse them permission, but neither enthusiasm nor age tells staff what they need to know. Even children who regularly use the shallow pool should be asked to show that they can manage the distance before they enter alone.

Which of the following best illustrates the principle underlying the above argument?

options.A: A sailing centre requires anyone taking a boat out alone to demonstrate that they can bring it safely back to the jetty.
options.B: A museum gives free entry to anyone who has visited during the previous month.
options.C: A school allows older pupils to borrow a different set of books.
options.D: A club gives everyone the same certificate after a safety talk, whether or not they took part.
options.E: A café asks some customers to pay in cash when the card terminal is broken.

questions.explanation: An activity posing a specific safety risk should be undertaken alone only after demonstrating the competence needed to manage that risk.

questions.stem:
A weekly paper has discovered that its front page last week gave a local society's membership as twenty when the correct number is two hundred. The paper will print the correct figure this week. The editor argues that putting it in a routine corrections box near the end would be insufficient, because many readers saw the front page without looking at the rest of the paper. The correction should appear where those who read the original figure are at least likely to see it, even though it needs only one line.

Which of the following best illustrates the principle underlying the above argument?

options.A: A teacher puts a student's corrected mark in a private file to protect the student's privacy.
options.B: A firm issues a detailed report to make its figures easier to compare across years.
options.C: A publisher fixes spelling in an unpublished draft before sending it for review.
options.D: A radio station repeats accurate advertisements at the times when its audience is largest.
options.E: A bus company corrects an incorrect destination notice on the same large display where passengers were given the wrong information.

questions.explanation: The principle is to make a correction visible to the people who encountered the error, not merely to put the correct information somewhere.

questions.stem:
A mine supervisor has two jobs to assign for the last hour of a shift. One is routine; the other requires entering a cramped inspection chamber. Two qualified workers are available, but one spent the first part of the day doing the same kind of awkward inspection and has just returned. Although both workers can formally be assigned to either job, the supervisor should give the chamber job to the one who has not yet done such work today. The inconvenient duties should be shared over time rather than simply assigned to whoever is closest.

Which of the following best illustrates the principle underlying the above argument?

options.A: A doctor with a rare qualification deals with all patients who need that qualification.
options.B: A shop chooses the person nearest the till to handle a long queue.
options.C: An office waives an inconvenient assignment for its longest-serving worker every month.
options.D: An organiser postpones an unnecessary job to avoid giving it to anybody.
options.E: Two equally trained carers are on duty; the one who did not work the previous overnight shift takes the next one rather than giving both to the other.

questions.explanation: The supervisor is distributing comparable burdens among people equally able to bear them. The overnight shift example applies that principle.

questions.stem:
An exhibition is lending signed ceramic dishes to restaurants for display. It is willing to let kitchen staff place ordinary plates near them, but does not want visibly similar copies put into circulation with the pottery's signature still on them. Many diners would have no way to know which dishes were copies if they were offered for sale later. The potter has no objection to reproduction as such. What matters is that an imitation that might be mistaken for an original be permanently marked as a reproduction before it leaves the workshop.

Which of the following best illustrates the principle underlying the above argument?

options.A: A mapmaker permits facsimiles of old survey sheets provided each carries a lasting label identifying it as a facsimile.
options.B: A chef reveals the ingredients of a dish only to diners who ask.
options.C: A gallery refuses to display any image unless the artist personally brings it.
options.D: A laboratory asks everyone to use identical labels so its bottles look uniform.
options.E: A printer increases the price of posters signed by their designer.

questions.explanation: The principle permits copies while requiring a durable distinction when they could otherwise pass as originals.

questions.stem:
When an island's main fuel delivery was cancelled, the distributor had enough stock for only half of its regular orders. It assigned fuel first to the community bus and the clinic, even though private buyers offered to pay a higher price. A single high bidder could have kept a spare generator running, but without the clinic generator or bus several residents would lose access to essential services. Normal prices can determine who gets fuel after supplies recover. During the shortage, however, keeping those services available should take priority over securing the largest immediate payment.

Which of the following best illustrates the principle underlying the above argument?

options.A: A shop sells scarce watches to its longest-standing customers, regardless of why they want them.
options.B: A charity accepts the highest offer for donated furniture to maximise its fundraising.
options.C: During a water shortage, a tanker serves a care home before a lucrative commercial booking whose cancellation will not endanger an essential service.
options.D: A transport office replaces a lightly used bus with a cheaper minibus outside peak hours.
options.E: A pharmacist saves goods for customers who have already paid rather than selling them again at a discount.

questions.explanation: The argument gives maintaining essential services priority over greater revenue when a resource is scarce. The tanker decision does that.

questions.stem:
A factory can reduce the noise reaching nearby apartments by fitting an enclosure to one press. Moving several tenants to flats farther away would also remove their exposure, at about the same cost to the factory. The residents did nothing to bring about the problem and have established ties in the area. They should not have to choose between keeping their homes and getting a quiet night when a remedy at the press is equally feasible. The fact that the factory could offer to cover the cost of each move does not settle where the remedy should be applied.

Which of the following best illustrates the principle underlying the above argument?

options.A: A council moves rubbish bins away from a road during planned resurfacing.
options.B: A bakery fits a hood to stop smoke reaching adjoining homes instead of paying those residents to relocate.
options.C: A resident rents out a flat to pay for quieter accommodation elsewhere.
options.D: Two households split the cost of a higher fence they both want.
options.E: A manufacturer takes back a faulty batch because no repair is possible.

questions.explanation: When a feasible remedy at the source exists, do not make those affected by the harm uproot themselves. Paying them to move does not answer that concern.

questions.stem:
A charity invited volunteers to be photographed for a printed report about a completed building project. Several agreed on the understanding that the photographs would accompany descriptions of their own work. The charity now wants to use the images in a fundraising advertisement for a different project. The images are already in its files and the campaign is for a good cause. Nevertheless, agreement to the first use should not be treated as permission for the second; the charity should ask again before placing anybody's photograph in the advertisement.

Which of the following best illustrates the principle underlying the above argument?

options.A: A photographer refuses to publish any pictures stored on a damaged memory card.
options.B: A school takes a new photo each year for cards pupils have already agreed to carry.
options.C: A research group asks participants before putting interview extracts in a public training film, although they had agreed to the extracts being used in an internal report.
options.D: A council repeats a public notice in two newspapers within one campaign.
options.E: A club keeps members' postal addresses up to date to send the newsletters they requested.

questions.explanation: Permission for a specific purpose should not be extended to a materially different use without new consent.

questions.stem:
A forecasting team asks its readers to trust a claim about the likely effect of a sea wall. The figures behind the claim were calculated with a model the team will not let independent engineers inspect. The figures may be right, and the team has a good record of accurate estimates. But an organisation deciding whether to pay for the wall would not be able to tell whether the model used assumptions appropriate to that stretch of coast. The findings should not be the decisive evidence for the expenditure while the basis for them remains unavailable for scrutiny.

Which of the following best illustrates the principle underlying the above argument?

options.A: A scientist declines to use a test because a rival laboratory devised it first.
options.B: A town declines to base a major bridge purchase solely on a test whose conditions its engineers cannot inspect, even though the tester is reputable.
options.C: A purchaser always buys the least expensive part even when its test results are independently verified.
options.D: An engineer prefers findings from a local test because the report is easier to read.
options.E: An organisation uses only research whose findings were published in the same year it makes its decision.

questions.explanation: A consequential decision should not rest decisively on a claim that cannot be independently scrutinised. Reputation alone does not remove that need.

questions.stem:
A regional poetry award pays its judges a flat fee, so a judge receives nothing extra if any particular poem wins. One judge has been tutoring a shortlisted poet for several years. The judge believes she can assess the poem impartially and may be right. The other entrants, however, have no way to check what weight she gives the tutoring relationship. She should step back from ranking that poem. The award needs to avoid a reasonable appearance of partiality as well as to prevent actual favouritism or a financial conflict.

Which of the following best illustrates the principle underlying the above argument?

options.A: A contest excludes judges who do not understand the eligibility rules.
options.B: A manager stays out of a vote entirely because the result will not affect her.
options.C: A hiring panel member does not interview a close friend, even though he could mark fairly and stands to gain nothing from the result.
options.D: A council lets each applicant check that their form was received.
options.E: A teacher awards a prize using objective marks after publicly comparing the work.

questions.explanation: A close relationship can create an apparent conflict even without actual bias or financial gain. Recusal protects confidence in the decision.

questions.stem:
A hall has one free evening that it can offer to either of two community groups. Both applied before the deadline, their proposals meet the published criteria equally well, and neither would have a practical advantage in using a different evening. The bookings manager has seen one of the groups perform and personally likes its work. Because that preference was never part of the criteria, it should not now determine the booking. Drawing a name at random gives each equally qualified group the same opportunity without introducing a criterion that applicants had not been told about.

Which of the following best illustrates the principle underlying the above argument?

options.A: A recruiter chooses the only applicant with a qualification that was required in the advert.
options.B: An organiser uses a raffle to pay for an award whose winner is selected by judges.
options.C: A charity lets its donors decide which of two unequal grant applications to support.
options.D: A venue gives a booking to the group that applied first under a published first-come rule.
options.E: Where two equally eligible tenants request the only spare storage unit, the landlord draws lots rather than choosing the tenant whose decorating she admires.

questions.explanation: When relevant published criteria do not distinguish candidates, an equal chance is preferable to an unrelated personal preference.

questions.stem:
At a repair café, spare parts are kept in drawers. The list gives drawer numbers, not quantities.
Part          | 12 mm | 16 mm | 20 mm
Rubber washer | 7     | 9     | 6
Steel washer  | 3     | 8     | 5
Locking ring  | 4     | 2     | 1
Where should a volunteer look for a 16 mm steel washer?
questions.explanation: Choose the steel washer row and the 16 mm column.

questions.stem:
A mobile greengrocer starts with £28 in the till. Before noon she receives £47 in cash and £63 in card payments, and gives a £9 cash refund.
How much cash is in the till at noon?
questions.explanation: Add cash receipts and subtract the refund from the opening cash. Card payments never enter the till.

questions.stem:
A chandlery labels part-used reels by the length of rope left: white for less than 5 m, pink for 5 to under 10 m, blue for 10 to under 15 m, black for 15 to under 20 m and orange for 20 m or more.
A 25 m reel has 10 m cut off it. Which label does it need?

options.A: Black
options.B: White
options.C: Pink
options.D: Blue
options.E: Orange

questions.explanation: There are 15 m left, which is the lower endpoint of the black band.

questions.stem:
A local archive accepts requests until 15:45, but its reading room stays open until 16:25. Rosa has already ordered her documents and sits down at 14:50.
How long can she use the documents before the room closes?
questions.explanation: The request deadline does not matter because the documents have been ordered. From 14:50 to 16:25 is 95 minutes.

questions.stem:
Before a garden show, a box of apples is weighed. The scale reads 7.6 kg. The empty box weighs 0.8 kg and its lid, which was on it, weighs 0.3 kg.
What is the weight of the apples alone?

options.A: 6.8 kg
options.B: 7.1 kg
options.C: 6.5 kg
options.D: 7.3 kg
options.E: 7.6 kg

questions.explanation: Subtract both the box and its lid: 7.6 − 0.8 − 0.3 = 6.5 kg.

questions.stem:
A pool counts only paid lessons when deciding whether instructors qualify for a bonus.
Instructor | Paid adults | Paid children | Free trials
Cal        | 12          | 15            | 4
Edi        | 19          | 6             | 9
Freya      | 10          | 19            | 1
Gus        | 14          | 14            | 6
Hana       | 18          | 10            | 4
Who taught the most lessons that count towards the bonus?

options.A: Cal
options.B: Freya
options.C: Edi
options.D: Gus
options.E: Hana

questions.explanation: Add the two paid columns only. Freya has 29 paid lessons; the next highest total is 28.

questions.stem:
Times below are minutes past 08:00. A shuttle passenger cannot board the 08:20 ferry unless they reach its gate by 08:17.
Stop         | Shuttle arrival | Walk to gate (min)
King's Steps | 14              | 3
Chapel       | 16              | 2
Docks        | 19              | 4
Mill         | 22              | 1
Bend         | 26              | 1
What is the latest shuttle stop arrival that still allows boarding?

options.A: King's Steps
options.B: Chapel
options.C: Docks
options.D: Mill
options.E: Bend

questions.explanation: The shuttle at King's Steps gets its passenger to the gate at 08:17. The 08:16 Chapel arrival still needs a two-minute walk.

questions.stem:
The choir paid for 45 seats on a coach. On the day, 32 of the original singers travel and 5 of the absent singers send a replacement, each of whom takes a seat.
The driver and conductor travel in separate front seats. How many of the 45 seats are empty?
questions.explanation: Only the 32 singers and five replacements use the paid seats. The difference between 45 and 37 is eight.

questions.stem:
A bike workshop bills labour at £8 for each 15 minutes or part of 15 minutes. Supplied brake blocks are £6 per pair and cables £4 each.
A job takes 32 minutes, needs one cable and uses the customer's own brake blocks. Find the bill.
questions.explanation: Round 32 minutes to three chargeable blocks. Add the £4 cable, but not brake blocks.

questions.stem:
A food hub runs two fridges. At noon the North fridge contained 18 cartons and the South fridge held 27. By closing, volunteers had moved 6 cartons from South to North, and visitors had taken 9 from North and 4 from South.
How many cartons remained in South?
questions.explanation: Start with the South fridge's 27 cartons and subtract both the six sent North and the four taken by visitors.

questions.stem:
This is the closing table of a five-team league. Teams are ranked first by points, then by goal difference (goals for minus goals against).
Team  | Points | For | Against
Alder | 21     | 29  | 16
Briar | 23     | 22  | 21
Cedar | 23     | 25  | 19
Dene  | 22     | 31  | 11
Elm   | 19     | 28  | 13
Which team finished second?

options.A: Alder
options.B: Briar
options.C: Cedar
options.D: Dene
options.E: Elm

questions.explanation: Only Briar and Cedar reached 23 points. Cedar's goal difference is larger, so Briar is second.

questions.stem:
A launderette lists powders as follows. The amounts of powder per wash are already allowed for in the number of washes.
Pack  | Weight | Washes | Price
Amber | 700 g  | 14     | £4.20
Birch | 900 g  | 18     | £5.04
Clove | 1 kg   | 25     | £7.50
Dulse | 1.2 kg | 24     | £6.96
Ember | 1.5 kg | 30     | £8.10
Which pack has the lowest price per wash?

options.A: Ember
options.B: Amber
options.C: Birch
options.D: Clove
options.E: Dulse

questions.explanation: Compare price divided by washes, not price divided by weight. The prices per wash are 30p, 28p, 30p, 29p and 27p.

questions.stem:
An orchard manager checks the change in temperature between dawn and noon.
Day       | Dawn | Noon | Evening
Monday    | −4°C | 3°C  | 2°C
Tuesday   | −1°C | 7°C  | 1°C
Wednesday | 3°C  | 9°C  | 2°C
Thursday  | 0°C  | 5°C  | −2°C
Friday    | −3°C | 4°C  | −4°C
Which day had the largest dawn-to-noon rise?

options.A: Monday
options.B: Wednesday
options.C: Thursday
options.D: Friday
options.E: Tuesday

questions.explanation: The rises, in order, were 7°C, 8°C, 6°C, 5°C and 7°C. The highest noon reading is not the biggest rise.

questions.stem:
A hall hires out the same five hourly slots, 09:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00 and 13:00, on Monday and Tuesday. On Monday 09:00 and 11:00 are booked; on Tuesday 10:00 and 11:00 are booked.
A tutor needs the same slot on both days, and neither lesson can start after 12:00. Which start should the tutor request?
questions.explanation: Cross out any slot which is booked on either day and cross out 13:00. Only 12:00 remains.

questions.stem:
A gallery wants a poster print that is at least 50 cm long, costs no more than £12 and is ready within four working days.
Printer | Length | Cost | Working days
Aster   | 52 cm  | £11  | 5
Broom   | 48 cm  | £10  | 3
Cress   | 50 cm  | £12  | 4
Dock    | 54 cm  | £13  | 2
Elder   | 49 cm  | £12  | 4
Which printer meets the brief?

options.A: Aster
options.B: Broom
options.C: Dock
options.D: Elder
options.E: Cress

questions.explanation: Cress meets all three limits exactly. Aster is too slow, Broom and Elder are too short, and Dock is too expensive.

questions.stem:
At Brook bridge a towpath forks. The north arm goes 600 m to a lock, then 450 m to a cottage. The south arm goes 300 m to a jetty, then 550 m to a weir. There are no other links.
What distance does a walker cover going from the jetty to the cottage by the towpath?
questions.explanation: From the jetty go back to the fork, then via the lock to the cottage. The three lengths are 300 m, 600 m and 450 m.

questions.stem:
A ranger checked 120 young trees. Of the 30 birches checked, 6 were damaged. Of the 90 other trees, 9 were damaged.
What percentage of the birches checked were damaged?
questions.explanation: Birches are the only relevant group. Six out of 30 is one fifth, or 20%.

questions.stem:
A bakery can display up to 60 pastries. Its costs per unsold pastry are 35p for a bun and 55p for a tart; selling prices are £1 and £2 respectively.
At closing the owner finds 7 buns, 4 tarts and 3 biscuits unsold. The biscuits were on sale on behalf of another baker, at no cost to this shop.
What is the cost to the shop of these unsold pastries, in pence?
questions.explanation: Only the bakery's own unsold items count. Their costs add to 245p + 220p = 465p.

questions.stem:
Each swimmer in a relay covers one length. Here are the cumulative times at the end of each leg, in seconds.
Team | Leg 1 | Leg 2 | Leg 3 | Leg 4
East | 37    | 71    | 110   | 145
West | 39    | 75    | 109   | 147
By how many seconds did East's final swimmer beat West's final swimmer?
questions.explanation: East's final leg took 35 seconds and West's took 38 seconds. The difference is three seconds, not the gap in the teams' finishing times.

questions.stem:
A hospital car park charges for each hour or part of an hour. The first two hours are £3 each; each subsequent hour is £2. Blue badge holders pay half the usual total.
A driver without a blue badge enters at 11:45 and leaves at 14:05. What is the charge?
questions.explanation: The stay is two hours and 20 minutes, charged as three hours. The first two cost £6 and the third costs £2.

questions.stem:
A shared office takes meter readings at the start and end of June. The closing readings are cumulative, not June-only totals.
Service     | Start | End | Price per unit
Electricity | 705   | 745 | 26p
Water       | 394   | 410 | 84p
Heating     | 911   | 932 | 32p
How many pence more was spent on water than on electricity during June?
questions.explanation: The office used 16 water units and 40 electricity units. The costs are 1,344p and 1,040p respectively.

questions.stem:
After a hailstorm a nursery writes off 10% of its 70 potted pears and 20% of its 30 potted plums. The apple trees are unaffected and have not been counted here.
Of the pear and plum trees together, what percentage was written off?
questions.explanation: Seven pears and six plums were written off. That is 13 out of 100 trees, not the average of the two percentages.

questions.stem:
A furniture shop's delivery charge depends on distance from the shop and on the heaviest piece. Several pieces incur one delivery charge.
Distance         | 20 kg or under | Over 20 kg
Up to 5 km       | £5             | £8
Over 5 to 10 km  | £8             | £12
Over 10 to 20 km | £11            | £16
Nell lives exactly 10 km away and buys a 13 kg chest, a 20 kg desk and a 2 kg lamp. What does she pay for delivery?
questions.explanation: Ten kilometres is in the middle band. The heaviest item is exactly 20 kg, so the lower charge applies.

questions.stem:
At a theatre, seats in a row are numbered 1 to 24. Seats 5 to 16 inclusive are under cover. Seats 1 to 8 and 19 to 24 are the budget seats.
How many budget seats in this row are not under cover?
questions.explanation: In the first budget block, seats 1 to 4 are uncovered. All six seats in the other budget block are uncovered, giving ten in total.

questions.stem:
These lab samples were either sent to storage or destroyed, never both. The blanks mean information not given.
Batch | Received | Stored | Destroyed
P     | 36       | 31     | —
Q     | —        | 28     | 8
R     | 50       | —      | 11
Combining all three batches, how many samples were stored?
questions.explanation: Batch R stored 39 of its 50 samples. Add that to the known stored counts of 31 and 28.

questions.stem:
A market requires five full intervening days between an application and trading. Applications are accepted every day except Sunday; the market itself runs only on Thursday.
If a trader wants a stall on Thursday 18 June, when is the latest application date?
questions.explanation: Applying on the 12th leaves the 13th to the 17th as five intervening days. A later application leaves fewer days.

questions.stem:
A delayed train traveller can claim half the fare for the affected leg, not half the cost of a return or any seat fees. A £44 return consists of a £26 outward fare and an £18 inward fare; two £3 seat fees are paid separately.
Only the inward service was delayed. How many pounds can the traveller claim?
questions.explanation: Half the inward fare of £18 is £9. Ignore the outward fare and both fees.

questions.stem:
A junior chess tournament admits players with 3 points or more who have played at least four rounds. A retired player's place cannot be awarded, even if they met both thresholds.
Name | Rounds | Points | Status
Ari  | 4      | 3      | Active
Bo   | 5      | 2.5    | Active
Cy   | 4      | 4      | Retired
Dee  | 3      | 3      | Active
Eve  | 5      | 3.5    | Active
How many of these players can be awarded a place?
questions.explanation: Only Ari and Eve meet both numerical thresholds and are still active.

questions.stem:
A café orders tonic by the crate, with 24 bottles in a crate. It has 31 bottles on hand but has set 12 of them aside for a private party.
The café wants 90 bottles available to ordinary customers after delivery. What is the least number of crates to order?
questions.explanation: There are only 19 usable bottles on hand, so 71 more are needed. Two crates give 48; three give 72.

questions.stem:
A crew considers only normal days when checking its typical recycling load. Its daily loads were as follows, in tonnes:
Day      | Mon | Tue | Wed | Thu | Fri | Sat | Sun
Load (t) | 8   | 11  | 6   | 14  | 9   | 20  | 10
Tuesday was affected by a breakdown and Saturday included an extra collection. What was the median of the normal days' loads?
questions.explanation: Remove Tuesday and Saturday, then sort the five remaining loads: 6, 8, 9, 10, 14. The middle value is 9.

questions.stem:
A bakery can only use a depot if its driver has five whole minutes or more between arriving there and its closing time.
Depot | Arrival | Closes
Bower | 10:03   | 10:08
Crane | 09:46   | 09:50
Dale  | 10:17   | 10:21
Fen   | 10:04   | 10:11
Grove | 09:29   | 09:34
Two of the depots are unavailable. Which two?

options.A: Bower and Grove
options.B: Crane and Dale
options.C: Crane and Fen
options.D: Dale and Fen
options.E: Fen and Grove

questions.explanation: Only Crane and Dale have fewer than five minutes left. Exactly five whole minutes is enough.

questions.stem:
A driver taking volunteers to a coastal clean-up must collect either Imani or Jo, then either Kit or Luz. Driving times in minutes are given below; there is no waiting.
Garage to Imani | 7 | Garage to Jo | 9
Imani to Kit    | 5 | Imani to Luz | 8
Jo to Kit       | 2 | Jo to Luz    | 4
Kit to beach    | 9 | Luz to beach | 6
How much longer is the slowest trip than the fastest?
questions.explanation: The four trips take 21, 21, 20 and 19 minutes. The difference between the longest and shortest is two minutes.

questions.stem:
At a station lockers of any size cost £3 to activate. During the first 24 hours the charge per six hours or part is £2 for a small locker and £4 for a large one.
Ola opens one small locker at 17:10 and leaves it closed until collecting everything at 06:45 next morning. How much is the charge?
questions.explanation: The stay is 13 hours and 35 minutes, or three chargeable blocks. Add the £3 activation charge to £6.

questions.stem:
Two buses have respectively 27 and 32 seats for passengers. Six seats in the larger bus have no seat belts; they may be used by adults but not by children. There are 4 adults and 49 children.
What is the greatest number of additional children who could travel on these buses?
questions.explanation: There are 53 belted seats. The four adults can use unbelted seats, leaving four belted seats after the 49 children sit down.

questions.stem:
A jam maker bottles 60 jars of plum, 40 of apple and 20 of quince. A trader buys 15 plum and 5 apple jars; 10 quince jars are then given away.
What fraction of the remaining jars contain apple jam?
questions.explanation: There are 35 apple jars among the 90 jars left altogether. Simplifying 35/90 gives 7/18.

questions.stem:
A cobbler's receipt separates labour, materials and delivery. A voucher takes 25% off labour only, but the resulting saving is limited to £9.
Repair | Labour | Materials | Delivery
Boots  | £24    | £13       | £4
Bag    | £20    | £5        | £4
The two repairs are paid for together on one receipt. What is the final bill?
questions.explanation: Total labour is £44, so the calculated saving is £11, capped at £9. The original £70 bill falls to £61.

questions.stem:
A caretaker takes the first bus that arrives before the building must be opened. The journey from the stop to the door takes exactly 7 minutes. The table lists buses that run on Wednesdays.
Bus arrival | Runs on public holidays?
07:41       | No
07:47       | Yes
07:54       | No
08:02       | Yes
08:10       | Yes
It is a public-holiday Wednesday and the door must open by 08:00. How many minutes early will the caretaker reach it?
questions.explanation: The first bus running that day arrives at 07:47. The walk ends at 07:54, six minutes early.

questions.stem:
A canteen has three tills. One serves a customer every 30 seconds and the other two each serve a customer every 45 seconds. All three begin serving at 12:00 and continue without a break.
From 12:00 to 12:04 inclusive, how many customers are served and have finished paying?
questions.explanation: The quick till completes eight payments. Each slower till completes five; the sixth at either would end after 12:04.

questions.stem:
A rescue team follows a path marked with five survey posts. Between neighbouring posts the path either rises or falls steadily.
Post     | P  | Q   | R   | S   | T
Height m | 90 | 155 | 112 | 168 | 137
The team walks from T to P, stopping briefly at every post. How many metres of ascent does the team make in total?
questions.explanation: Walking back along the list, the rises are T to S (31 m) and R to Q (43 m). The other two stages are descents.

questions.stem:
A cooperative pays farmers by accepted weight: grade A gets £5 per kg, grade B £3. Rejected grain earns nothing, and a £4 testing charge is deducted once per farmer.
Bag | Grade | Weight | Rejected
1   | A     | 12 kg  | 2 kg
2   | B     | 15 kg  | 3 kg
3   | A     | 7 kg   | 1 kg
How much does the farmer receive?
questions.explanation: There are 16 accepted kilos at £5 and 12 at £3. Deduct the single £4 testing charge from £116.

questions.stem: A kiosk charges 65p for a postcard. A customer pays with £1. The kiosk gives change in 20p, 10p and 5p coins only, and has no shortage of any of them. What is the fewest coins the customer can receive?
questions.explanation: One 20p, one 10p and one 5p make 35p. No pair among these denominations has a total of 35p.

questions.stem: A rectangular display board is 90 cm wide and 60 cm high. A ribbon is to run around its perimeter, except for a 20 cm opening along one edge. The ribbon will not overlap at the corners. What length is needed?
questions.explanation: The full perimeter is 300 cm. Subtract the 20 cm opening.

questions.stem: The first bread of the day must be ready to slice at 07:30. After it is put in the oven it bakes for 38 minutes, rests in the tin for 7 minutes and then cools on a rack for 25 minutes. At what time must it go in the oven?
questions.explanation: The three stages take 70 minutes in total. Count back 70 minutes from 07:30.

questions.stem: A radio club has 47 rechargeable batteries, of which 8 fail a test and must be discarded. Each working radio requires exactly 4 batteries. If the club equips as many radios as it can, how many tested working batteries are left unused?
questions.explanation: There are 39 working batteries. Nine sets of four use 36, leaving three.

questions.stem: Five collectors each give one card to every other collector. Each card is written by one person and delivered to one other person. How many cards change hands?
questions.explanation: Each of the five collectors gives four cards. Giving in opposite directions counts as two cards.

questions.stem: A café sells tea for £2 a cup and coffee for £3 a cup. One table orders seven drinks and pays exactly £17 for them. How many teas did they order?
questions.explanation: Seven teas would be £14. Each switch from tea to coffee adds £1, so there were three coffees and four teas.

questions.stem: A maker draws a fabric canopy at a scale of 1 cm to 40 cm. On the drawing one seam is 7.5 cm long. The fabric must be cut 10 cm longer than the seam for hemming. How long, in metres, should the maker cut it?
questions.explanation: The real seam is 300 cm, and the allowance brings the cut to 310 cm, or 3.1 metres.

questions.stem: Tom reads 8 pages on Monday. Each day through Friday he reads three more pages than he did the previous day. How many pages does he read over the five days?
questions.explanation: The daily amounts are 8, 11, 14, 17 and 20. Their total is 70.

questions.stem: In a window display a panel is made up of 8 columns and 7 rows of square tiles. The maker removes a 3-by-2 rectangle of tiles and then takes away one other tile for a cable. How many tiles are left?
questions.explanation: Start with 56 tiles and subtract six for the rectangle and one for the cable.

questions.stem: A display lamp cycles through white, blue, amber, green and red, then repeats. It is now amber. Each press of the button moves it forward by one colour. What colour will it be after 18 presses?

options.A: Blue
options.B: Amber
options.C: Green
options.D: Red
options.E: White

questions.explanation: Fifteen presses return to amber. The three remaining presses go green, red, then white.

questions.stem: A textile shop sends exactly 28 rolls to a warehouse. A parcel holds either 4 rolls or 6 rolls, and all parcels must be full. There are only two 6-roll parcels available. What is the least number of parcels the shop can send?
questions.explanation: Using two sixes leaves 16 rolls, which fill four fours. Zero sixes gives seven parcels and one six leaves a non-multiple of four.

questions.stem: A storeroom lock takes a two-digit code with a non-zero tens digit. The digits sum to 11. Reversing them makes a number 27 greater than the code. What is the original code?
questions.explanation: Reversing the digits adds nine times the difference between them. The digits therefore differ by three and sum to eleven, with the smaller first.

questions.stem: A weather vane fitted for a play points east when a scene starts. It then turns a quarter turn clockwise, a half turn anticlockwise and three eighths of a turn clockwise, viewed from above. Which direction does it finally point?

options.A: South-east
options.B: North-east
options.C: East
options.D: South
options.E: South-west

questions.explanation: Counting in eighth turns, the net movement is one eighth clockwise. From east this gives south-east.

questions.stem: For a night walk, each of four beginners needs a separate guide. The names of the only guides with whom each beginner is comfortable are listed below. Ivy and Kai can go with Uma only; Leo can go with Val or Wen; Mina can go with Wen or Zan. What is the greatest number of beginners who can take part?
questions.explanation: Ivy and Kai cannot both take part because only Uma can guide either. One of them can walk with Uma while Leo and Mina go with two other guides.

questions.stem: A community radio show starts on Monday 6 April and returns exactly every 9 days. Its producer records an extra introduction whenever a show falls on a Friday. Including the launch as show 1, which show first needs the introduction?
questions.explanation: A gap of nine days moves the show forward two weekdays. The first three shows fall on Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

questions.stem: Of 48 outdoor-cinema guests, 31 hired a blanket, 26 bought a hot drink and 8 did neither. How many guests both hired a blanket and bought a drink?
questions.explanation: Forty guests did at least one. Adding the two counts gives 57, with the people who did both counted twice.

questions.stem: Two walkers set out 15 km apart on the same straight trail and walk towards one another. Nia starts at 08:00 at 3 km/h; Ollie starts at 09:00 at 5 km/h. At what time do they meet?
questions.explanation: At 09:00 the walkers are 12 km apart. They close the gap at 8 km/h, so the meeting is 90 minutes later.

questions.stem: For every instrument it ships, a workshop needs two foam blocks and one crate. It starts with 19 blocks and 13 crates. It can buy packets of three blocks, or extra crates singly. What is the fewest purchases (packets or single crates) needed to ship 14 instruments?
questions.explanation: Fourteen instruments need 28 blocks, so nine more means three packs. They also need one extra crate.

questions.stem: A clock in a walled garden keeps perfect time. Its hands move continuously. What is the smaller angle between the hands at 04:20?
questions.explanation: At 04:20 the minute hand is on the 4. The hour hand has moved one third of the 30° gap towards 5, so the hands differ by 10°.

questions.stem: A costume maker has six swatches, no two alike. Three are red shades and three blue. She chooses two swatches to pin to a board, in no particular order. The selection cannot contain two reds. How many possibilities are there?
questions.explanation: There are 15 unordered pairs. Remove the three pairs formed entirely from red swatches.

questions.stem: An empty tank holds 360 litres. A wide pipe fills it at 24 litres per minute but is closed after the first five minutes. A narrow pipe, opened just as the wide one closes, fills it at 15 litres per minute. How many minutes does filling take altogether?
questions.explanation: The first five minutes supply 120 litres. The remaining 240 litres take another 16 minutes.

questions.stem: A restorer examines a tray of tiles. She rejects a quarter of them immediately, then rejects a third of the tiles left. There are 18 good tiles. How many tiles were on the tray before she examined any?
questions.explanation: The good tiles are two thirds of the three quarters kept initially. That is half the original tray, so the tray started with 36.

questions.stem: A paper square is divided into a four-by-four grid. A pupil folds its left half onto its right half, then its bottom half onto its top half. She punches through all layers at the centre of the top-right cell of the folded packet. After unfolding, how many of the holes are in corner cells of the original grid?
questions.explanation: The two folds reflect the punched cell into the other three corners. Each of the four holes lies in a corner cell.

questions.stem: A reserve has paths from the entrance to Pond (6 min) and Bank (5 min), from Pond to the hide (10 min), and from Bank to the hide (8 min). Pond and Bank are linked by a 2-minute path. All paths work both ways, and the entrance–Bank path has just closed. What is the quickest time from the entrance to the hide?
questions.explanation: The routes left are directly via Pond and via Pond then Bank. Both take 16 minutes.

questions.stem: A warehouse trolley has either three or five wheels. There are 14 trolleys in the dispatch area, with 58 wheels in all. No wheels are missing. How many are five-wheel trolleys?
questions.explanation: Fourteen three-wheel trolleys would account for 42 wheels. Each five-wheel trolley adds two more, making eight of that kind.

questions.stem: Two residents survey bats along the same street. Farah does every fourth evening and Gideon every sixth evening. Farah starts this evening; Gideon starts two evenings from now. After how many evenings, counting this evening as zero, do they first survey together?
questions.explanation: Farah works on evenings 0, 4, 8 and so on. Gideon works on 2, 8 and so on, so their first common evening is 8.

questions.stem: Ten seed trays gave an average of 14 seedlings per tray. Four of the trays were kept in a cold frame and averaged 8 seedlings each. Assuming every tray belongs to one of these two groups, what was the average number of seedlings in the six other trays?
questions.explanation: Subtract the cold frame's 32 seedlings from the overall 140. Divide the remaining 108 among six trays.

questions.stem: At a beach a wetsuit costs £9 for the first hour and £4 per additional hour. The hire shop never charges more than £25 in one day. Hires are in whole hours. What is the shortest hire for which the capped price is charged?
questions.explanation: After the initial £9, four further hours add £16. The cap is first reached at five hours.

questions.stem: A guide prints codes of three different letters chosen from J, K, L, M and N. A code cannot begin with J or end with N. How many different codes can be printed?
questions.explanation: Of the 60 unrestricted codes, 12 begin with J and 12 end with N. The three with both restrictions were subtracted twice, leaving 39.

questions.stem: A reservoir contains 150 litres. A tap adds 16 litres per minute while a leak removes 4 litres per minute. After three minutes the tap is turned off and the leak continues. How many minutes after the start will the level first fall to 162 litres?
questions.explanation: At shutoff the level is 186 litres. The leak then takes six more minutes to remove 24 litres.

questions.stem: A grower takes full baskets of two sizes to a market. Small baskets contain 9 plums and large baskets 14. There are at most four large baskets. Which total number of plums could NOT have been taken?
questions.explanation: With zero to four large baskets, reaching 70 would leave 70, 56, 42, 28 or 14 plums for small baskets. None of those remainders is a multiple of nine.

questions.stem: A sealed box weighs 16 kg. You have one weight each of 1 kg, 4 kg and 10 kg. On a balance you may put weights on either pan and leave some unused. Which additional weight would NOT enable you to balance the box?
questions.explanation: A second 4 kg weight cannot work: with the 10 kg weight opposite the box, the other three weights cannot provide a net 6 kg. The other options can complete 16 as 10 + 4 + 2, 10 + 4 + 3 − 1, 10 + 5 + 1 or 10 + 6.

questions.stem: A glazier needs at least 26 panes. A pack of six costs £18, a pack of ten £26 and loose panes cost £4 each. The glazier has space to take at most 28 panes. What is the least possible cost?
questions.explanation: Two packs of ten and one of six cost £70. With one or no ten-packs, reaching 26 costs more, and three ten-packs would exceed capacity.

questions.stem: Six people offer to paint a wall. Ava will not work with Bea; Bea will not work with Caz; Caz will not work with Dan; Dan will not work with Eli; Eli will not work with Flo; Flo will not work with Ava. All other pairs will work together. How many different largest groups can the organiser put together?
questions.explanation: Each included person rules out the next person around the six-person cycle, so at most three can be chosen. At size three the only choices alternate around the cycle, giving two groups.

questions.stem:
A tram leaves Oak at 17:04 and then every 12 minutes. It reaches Birch after nine minutes. The bus from Birch leaves every 15 minutes from 17:02 onward. Changing requires at least four minutes.
Jo reaches Oak at 17:13 and takes the first possible tram. How long does it take from reaching Oak to the departure of the bus Jo can first catch?
questions.explanation: The 17:16 tram arrives at 17:25. A transfer is possible from 17:29 onwards, so the 17:32 bus leaves 19 minutes after Jo reached Oak.

questions.stem: Parcel labels are all three-digit numbers from 200 to 299 inclusive. A label passes a check exactly when the sum of its three digits is a multiple of five. How many labels pass?
questions.explanation: For each of the ten possible tens digits, two of the ten units digits give the required remainder modulo five. That gives 20 labels.

questions.stem: A rectangular parcel measures 20 cm by 30 cm by 40 cm. Three separate loops of string are put round it, one around each of the three possible rectangular cross-sections parallel to a face. Each loop uses an extra 8 cm for a knot. How much string is used altogether?
questions.explanation: The loops have bare lengths of 100 cm, 120 cm and 140 cm. Add 24 cm for the three knots.

questions.stem: A council motion needs at least two thirds of votes cast, with no abstentions among those voting. There are currently 14 votes in favour and 9 against. Only additional supporters arrive and vote. How many of them must vote for the motion to pass?
questions.explanation: If four more supporters vote, the result is 18 out of 27, exactly two thirds. Three more support it only 17 out of 26.

questions.stem: An open day offers morning sessions in pottery, glass and weaving, and afternoon sessions in glass, weaving, metalwork and woodwork. A visitor chooses one of each but cannot repeat a craft, and people doing morning pottery cannot choose afternoon woodwork because the rooms are too far apart. How many different bookings are possible?
questions.explanation: Start with 12 pairs. Remove two craft repeats and the pottery–woodwork pair.

questions.stem: An exhibition guide numbers all its pages consecutively from 1 to 135. The designer discovers that the digit 4 is misprinted wherever it appears in a page number. How many separate misprinted digits are there?
questions.explanation: The units digit is 4 on 14 pages, and the tens digit is 4 on ten pages. On page 44 both positions count, giving 24 occurrences in all.

questions.stem: A drinks stall can buy at most 40 bottles from a supplier. The first 25 cost £2 each and any further bottles cost £1 each. The stall knows it can sell exactly 32 bottles at £4 each if it buys enough; any surplus is returned for 50p each. What is the greatest profit?
questions.explanation: Each sale adds more than its purchase cost, but a returned bottle loses 50p. Buying exactly 32 therefore gives £128 in sales less £57 in costs.

questions.stem: In a warehouse a trolley must move four aisles east and two rows north, one move at a time. It never moves west or south. For safety it cannot make its two northward moves consecutively. How many routes are allowed?
questions.explanation: Put the four east moves in order first; there are five gaps including both ends. Choose two different gaps for north moves, giving ten choices.

questions.stem: Three tanks P, Q and R cannot be weighed alone. On the same scale, P and Q together weigh 54 kg, P and R weigh 67 kg and Q and R weigh 73 kg. How much heavier is the heaviest tank than the lightest?
questions.explanation: The pair totals together count each tank twice, so all three weigh 97 kg. Subtracting the three pair totals in turn gives single weights of 43, 30 and 24 kg.

questions.stem: Four square tiles, all different, fill a two-by-two display frame. Moving the whole frame through a quarter turn does not make a new arrangement. A mirror image does make a new arrangement. How many arrangements are possible?
questions.explanation: Fix one particular tile at the top left by turning the frame. The three other distinct tiles can then be ordered in six ways.

questions.stem: A dark cupboard contains 7 batteries of type X, 5 of type Y and 4 of type Z. You cannot tell their type by touch, and none is replaced once taken. What is the least number you must take to guarantee two of type Y?
questions.explanation: In the worst case the first 12 batteries are all 11 non-Y batteries and one Y. The next one must be another Y.

questions.stem: An instrument counter has slots numbered 1 to 36. The pointer is at a slot whose number leaves remainder 2 when divided by 5 and remainder 4 when divided by 7. Which slot is it at?
questions.explanation: The candidates ending in 2 or 7 are 2, 7, 12, 17, 22, 27 and 32. Only 32 leaves remainder 4 after division by 7.

questions.stem:
A cube is folded from the net below. Each letter marks a square and each dot marks an empty position.

· E · ·
A B C D
· F · ·

Which face is opposite A on the completed cube?

options.A: B
options.B: D
options.C: C
options.D: E
options.E: F

questions.explanation: Fold up around B: A and C become the left and right faces. D folds round to face away from B.

questions.stem: At a qualifying race there are six finishers, with no ties. Theo finishes ahead of Uma, and Uma ahead of Val. Val is not last. What is the lowest position Theo could finish in?
questions.explanation: At least Uma, Val and a finisher behind Val have to follow Theo. Third is possible with the other two finishers ahead of him.

questions.stem: A stage lift can carry at most 123 kg. It must carry a 27 kg trolley and three instrument cases together. Each case weighs a whole number of kilograms, but the scales round to the nearest 5 kg and show 20 kg, 35 kg and 45 kg. If the combined load is within the lift's limit, what is the greatest possible exact weight of the heaviest case?
questions.explanation: The two lighter cases can weigh as little as 18 kg and 33 kg. Even then, after adding the trolley, there is only 45 kg left for the heaviest case.

questions.stem: Five distinct pictures are put in a row. A landscape must have exactly two pictures between it and a portrait. The other three pictures can go anywhere. How many arrangements satisfy the rule?
questions.explanation: The two special pictures can occupy positions 1 and 4 or 2 and 5, in either order. For each of the four placements there are six orders of the remaining pictures.

questions.stem: A decorator's sample uses 6 spoonfuls of blue pigment, 9 of white and 12 of grey. The decorator wants a larger batch of exactly the same mixture. The options give spoonfuls of blue, white and grey, in that order. Which batch will match?
questions.explanation: Reduce the original to 2:3:4. The batch with 12 blue, 18 white and 24 grey reduces to that ratio.

questions.stem:
A pedestrian trail is surveyed at successive posts. Their heights in metres are 88, 94, 92 and 97.
Which sequence of heights would give the same rises and falls between successive posts on another trail?
questions.explanation: The rises and falls are +6, −2 and +5 metres. The sequence starting at 107 has exactly those changes.

questions.stem:
In a trial, an observer recorded how many ants crossed a line in each of seven minutes.
Ants in a minute  | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3
Number of minutes | 1 | 2 | 3 | 1
One option could be the original seven readings in time order. Which is it?
questions.explanation: The list must contain one zero, two ones, three twos and one three. Their order within the list does not matter.

questions.stem: Four photographs were hung in this order from left to right: second largest, smallest, largest, second smallest. Five displays of different-sized postcards are proposed. Their widths in centimetres are listed from left to right. In which display are the relative sizes in the same order?
questions.explanation: The required width ranks from smallest are 3, 1, 4, 2. The widths 16, 9, 21, 12 give those ranks.

questions.stem: Of the votes at a club meeting, 45 were for a garden, 30 for a skittle alley and 15 for a games room. A pie chart shows only these votes. The options list its angles for garden, skittle alley and games room respectively. Which pie chart is accurate?
questions.explanation: The vote counts are in the ratio 3:2:1. A full circle has 360°, so the angles are 180°, 120° and 60°.

questions.stem: At a market stall, any £20 bowl is temporarily priced at £15. A nearby shop wants a discount with the same effect on the original price of every item, whatever that price is. Which offer does this?

options.A: Pay one fifth of the original price
options.B: Take 20% off the original price
options.C: Pay for two thirds of the original price
options.D: Take 25% off the original price
options.E: Take one sixth off the original price

questions.explanation: The reduced bowl price is three quarters of the original. Taking 25% off multiplies any original price by three quarters.

questions.stem:
A tap fills a tank, which is empty before the first minute. It adds these volumes in the first four minutes:
Minute       | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4
Litres added | 3 | 5 | 2 | 6
Which sequence gives the four readings at the end of the minutes on a gauge measuring total litres in the tank?
questions.explanation: Gauge totals accumulate the minute-by-minute additions. Add 3, then 5, then 2, then 6 to get 3, 8, 10 and 16.

questions.stem: A sign painter lays out three marks on a square board. Measured from its centre, the star is two squares north and the dot one square east; a cross is at the centre. The painter turns the board a quarter turn clockwise while looking down at it. Which description then fits the star and dot, in that order?

options.A: 2 north; 1 west
options.B: 2 east; 1 north
options.C: 2 west; 1 south
options.D: 2 east; 1 south
options.E: 2 south; 1 east

questions.explanation: A clockwise quarter turn moves north to east and east to south. The distances from the centre do not change.

questions.stem:
A hive sensor displayed these Celsius readings, but a calibration check found it read exactly 3°C too high at every time.
Hour    | 07:00 | 09:00 | 11:00 | 13:00
Reading | 12    | 15    | 18    | 17
Which set of readings would a correctly calibrated sensor have displayed?
questions.explanation: Subtract three degrees from every entry. The changes between readings are unaffected.

questions.stem: A customer buying cut timber pays one £7 setup charge per order and £3 per cut. An order with no cuts still incurs the setup charge. Which list of charges for zero, one and two cuts, in that order, shows this rule?
questions.explanation: The no-cut charge is £7. Each cut adds another £3, giving £10 and £13 for one and two cuts.

questions.stem:
A bookshop made a dot plot of the books bought by each of nine customers. There were two dots above 1, four above 2, one above 3 and two above 4.
Another shop had the same median and the same most common number of books per customer. Which set of sales could be from that shop?
questions.explanation: In the dot plot, the fifth dot is at 2 and the tallest stack is at 2. Only the list with four twos and containing a five has both properties.

questions.stem: In a practical test, a winch reels in 9 metres of rope in 24 seconds at a constant speed. A table of another winch's test results gives elapsed time followed by distance. Which row could show exactly the same speed?

options.A: 20 seconds, 7.5 metres
options.B: 12 seconds, 6 metres
options.C: 15 seconds, 5 metres
options.D: 18 seconds, 10.5 metres
options.E: 30 seconds, 12 metres

questions.explanation: The first winch moves 3 metres in 8 seconds. In 20 seconds it would move 7.5 metres, the same rate.

questions.stem:
A graph of a harbour's water level rises from noon to 13:00, stays level to 14:00, falls to 15:00 and rises to 16:00. There are no changes of direction within these one-hour intervals.
Which list of five readings, one on each hour from noon, could have produced this graph?
questions.explanation: Compare each reading with the previous one. The correct list goes up, stays the same, goes down, then goes up.

questions.stem: A bus shelter diagram has a lamp three metres north of its centre and two metres west of it. To put the shelter on the other side of a north–south road, the designer reflects the diagram in a north–south line through the centre, then translates it to its new location. Where is the lamp relative to the new centre?

options.A: 2 m west and 3 m south
options.B: 2 m east and 3 m north
options.C: 2 m east and 3 m south
options.D: 2 m west and 3 m north
options.E: 3 m east and 2 m north

questions.explanation: The reflection exchanges east and west and preserves north and south. Translation moves the lamp and centre together.

questions.stem: A cycling app reports a rider's steady pace as 4 minutes per kilometre. Another app displays speeds on a horizontal scale in kilometres per hour. At which mark should it put this rider's result?
questions.explanation: At one kilometre per four minutes, an hour contains 15 such intervals. The speed is 15 kilometres per hour.

questions.stem: A mural contains three solid squares with sides of 2, 3 and 4 metres. Printed sample charts give the areas of their three squares in square centimetres, from smallest to largest. Which chart could represent the mural at a single scale?
questions.explanation: Squaring the side lengths gives area ratio 4:9:16. The areas 12, 27 and 48 reduce to this ratio.

questions.stem: A press produces the same amount of oil for every kilogram of a particular kind of olive. It produces 18 litres from 60 kilograms. Which of these straight-line graph descriptions correctly shows its output?

options.A: Starts at 0 L for 0 kg and reaches 8 L for 20 kg
options.B: Starts at 3 L for 0 kg and reaches 9 L for 30 kg
options.C: Starts at 0 L for 0 kg and reaches 6 L for 25 kg
options.D: Starts at 0 L for 0 kg and reaches 14 L for 35 kg
options.E: Starts at 0 L for 0 kg and reaches 12 L for 40 kg

questions.explanation: There is no oil at zero kilograms, and the press produces three litres per ten kilograms. The matching line starts at zero and reaches 12 litres at 40 kilograms.

questions.stem: For a chemical sample to fit inside a tube, its length in centimetres must be less than 4.2. Records are now taken in millimetres, with lengths recorded as whole numbers of millimetres and no rounding necessary. Which new rule accepts exactly the same samples?

options.A: At most 40 mm
options.B: At most 42 mm
options.C: At most 43 mm
options.D: At most 44 mm
options.E: At most 41 mm

questions.explanation: The original rule excludes 42 mm itself. Among whole millimetres, 41 mm is therefore the greatest length allowed.

questions.stem:
A mill's three storage bins held 20 kg, 35 kg and 45 kg on Monday morning. Workers rearranged some grain between the bins but neither added nor removed any. By evening the largest bin held 8 kg more than it had in the morning.
Which evening inventory is consistent with this account? The bins appear in the same order, with the largest last.
questions.explanation: The total must still be 100 kg and the last bin must hold 53 kg. Only the inventory 12, 35, 53 satisfies both conditions.

questions.stem: A floor inlay occupies the cells (1, 1), (2, 1), (3, 1) and (3, 2) of a square grid. Coordinates increase to the right and upwards. A maker can slide or rotate this design but cannot turn it over. Which group of cells can it cover?
questions.explanation: A clockwise quarter turn places the shorter arm to the right of the bottom cell in the vertical run. Sliding gives the group at (2, 2), (2, 3), (2, 4) and (3, 2).

questions.stem: Three rooms at an animal shelter form a triangle, with a door joining every pair. One of those rooms also has a door to a fourth room; the fourth room has no other doors. Each option lists all two-way paths connecting four campsites, with PQ meaning that P and Q are linked directly. Which list has the same pattern of links as the shelter's rooms?

options.A: PQ, PR, QR, QS
options.B: PQ, QR, RS, SP
options.C: PQ, PR, PS
options.D: PQ, QR, RS
options.E: PQ, PR, PS, QR, RS

questions.explanation: P, Q and R must all connect to one another while just one of them connects to S. The list PQ, PR, QR, QS has that pattern.

questions.stem: One chart reports that a library extended its collection from 80 to 100 large-print books. A second chart tracks the number of graphic novels. Which pair of values, in order from before to after, gives the same percentage increase rather than the same number of extra books?
questions.explanation: The first increase is 20 out of 80, or one quarter. An increase from 48 to 60 is also one quarter of the starting number.

questions.stem: Five apprentices took 10, 10, 14, 16 and 20 minutes to finish a practice task. A second group has six apprentices. Which list could be its times if its mean time is the same but its median time is strictly higher?
questions.explanation: The first group's mean and median are both 14. The list with 8, 10, 15, 16, 17 and 18 totals 84 and has a median of 15.5.

questions.stem: At a river barrier 6 of 15 fish counted in the morning were salmon, and 9 of 20 counted in the afternoon were salmon. A report combines both samples in one headline. Which headline represents the combined result exactly?

options.A: 3 out of every 7 fish counted were salmon
options.B: 2 out of every 5 fish counted were salmon
options.C: 9 out of every 20 fish counted were salmon
options.D: 17 out of every 40 fish counted were salmon
options.E: 3 out of every 8 fish counted were salmon

questions.explanation: The combined count is 15 salmon out of 35 fish. Dividing both counts by five gives three out of seven.

questions.stem: A safety strip across a walkway starts at the left wall. It has a 2 m dark band, a 3 m pale band, another 2 m dark band and finally a 1 m pale band. A surveyor sets position zero at the right wall and measures back towards the left. In increasing order, at which positions does the colour change?
questions.explanation: From the right, the first band is 1 m wide, then come bands of 2 m and 3 m. So changes occur at 1, 3 and 6 m.

questions.stem:
The leisure centre counted the number of sessions booked by each of 20 households in one month.
Sessions per household | 0 | 1–2 | 3–4 | 5–6
Number of households   | 3 | 7   | 8   | 2
A report converts a figure from the table into a proportion. Which statement must be true?

options.A: Exactly 35% of households booked two sessions
options.B: Exactly 40% booked more than four sessions
options.C: Exactly three quarters booked at least one session
options.D: Exactly half booked fewer than two sessions
options.E: Exactly half booked at least three sessions

questions.explanation: The two groups from three to six sessions contain ten households altogether. The grouped data do not give exact counts for one and two sessions separately.

questions.stem: A theatre exchange desk swaps exactly three yellow tokens for one purple token or one purple for three yellow. The customer begins with 12 yellow and 3 purple. Which balance of yellow and purple, in that order, can the customer obtain by exchanges only?
questions.explanation: Treat every purple token as three yellow ones. An exchange leaves the total of 21 yellow-equivalents unchanged; only 3 yellow and 6 purple also give 21.

questions.stem: A jeweller strings six beads on a circular cord. Read clockwise from a jade bead, the order is jade, amber, jade, coral, amber, pearl. A customer may turn the necklace on the table but may not flip it. Which clockwise listing could describe the same necklace?

options.A: amber – pearl – jade – amber – jade – coral
options.B: amber – pearl – jade – amber – coral – jade
options.C: amber – jade – pearl – coral – jade – amber
options.D: amber – jade – amber – coral – jade – pearl
options.E: amber – pearl – coral – jade – amber – jade

questions.explanation: Begin at the amber immediately before the pearl. Continuing clockwise gives amber, pearl, jade, amber, jade, coral.

questions.stem:
A studio records five cues, A to E. A comes before C, C comes before E, and D comes before B. There are no other restrictions.
An automated scheduler is given two lists. It must keep the letters in each list in the order shown, but may interleave the lists in any way. Which pair of lists permits exactly the same schedules?

options.A: AEC / DB
options.B: ACE / BD
options.C: ACD / BE
options.D: ACE / DB
options.E: ABCDE / no second list

questions.explanation: The first list must enforce A before C before E. The other list must enforce D before B without restricting where those cues fall among the first three.

questions.stem: A station charges £4 to set up a sponsorship and £6 for each block of up to three episodes. Each option describes a rival station's invoice for a sponsorship of 1 to 12 episodes. Which rule gives the same charges throughout that range?

options.A: £8 for episodes 1–2, adding £4 at the start of each further 2-episode block
options.B: £16 for episodes 1–6, adding £12 at the start of each further 6-episode block
options.C: £10 for episodes 1–3, adding £6 at the start of each further 3-episode block
options.D: £10 for episodes 1–3, adding £10 at the start of each further 3-episode block
options.E: £10 for episodes 1–3, adding £8 at the start of each further 3-episode block

questions.explanation: Up to three episodes cost £10. The invoice rises by £6 at episodes 4, 7 and 10, so the matching rule has three-episode steps and starts at £10.

questions.stem:
A postal van's tachograph starts at 0 minutes at the depot. Its trip meter already shows 6 km at that point. At the roadside stops it shows:
Stop             | 1  | 2  | 3
Elapsed time min | 8  | 17 | 24
Trip meter km    | 10 | 16 | 21
Which record gives the time and distance for each of the three individual legs, in order?

options.A: 8 min, 4 km; 9 min, 6 km; 7 min, 5 km
options.B: 8 min, 10 km; 9 min, 6 km; 7 min, 5 km
options.C: 8 min, 4 km; 17 min, 10 km; 24 min, 15 km
options.D: 8 min, 4 km; 9 min, 5 km; 7 min, 6 km
options.E: 8 min, 6 km; 9 min, 4 km; 7 min, 5 km

questions.explanation: Take differences between consecutive readings in both rows, including the two starting readings. The legs are 8 minutes and 4 km, 9 minutes and 6 km, then 7 minutes and 5 km.

questions.stem: Two stage trolleys start at the same spot facing north. In the movement codes below, a number means drive that many metres straight ahead, and L and R mean turn a quarter turn left or right without moving. The first trolley uses code 3 R 2 R 1 L. Which code would put the second in exactly the same place, facing the same way?

options.A: 2 R 2 R
options.B: 2 L 2 R R
options.C: 1 R 2 L 1 L
options.D: 3 R 1 R 1 L

questions.explanation: The first trolley finishes two metres north and two east of its starting point, facing east. Going 2, turning right and going 2 reaches that position on the same heading.

questions.stem: A print firm sells posters at £8, £12, £16, £20 or £24. Its web checkout adds £4 to every price for delivery, then takes £6 off if the poster itself cost at least £20. Which shop-window rule gives every poster the same delivered price as the web checkout?

options.A: Add £4 below £20; at £20 or above, take off £2
options.B: Add £4 below £20; at £20 or above, take off £6
options.C: Add £4 below £16; at £16 or above, take off £2
options.D: Add £4 below £24; at £24 or above, take off £2
options.E: Add £4 below £20; at £20 or above, add £2

questions.explanation: The website charges £12, £16 and £20 for the first three prices and £18 and £22 for the other two. Only the rule that applies a net £2 reduction from a £20 tag onward matches all five.

questions.stem:
Three motion cameras watch consecutively numbered markers along a path. Camera A covers 5 to 9, B covers 1 to 6 and C covers 3 to 7, with endpoints included.
A summary gives these numbers in order: markers covered by all three; markers covered by A and B but not C; markers covered by exactly one camera. Which summary is right?
questions.explanation: Markers 5 and 6 are seen by all three, so A and B have no overlap outside C. The markers covered once are 1, 2, 8 and 9.

questions.stem: A rehearsal studio hires instruments out in sets of four. The first instrument in each set costs £2 to hire and the other three cost £5 apiece. Tuning costs a further £3, charged once per booking. A rival hires instruments singly but gives a discount on each complete group of four in an order. Which proposal makes its bill the same for every whole number of sets?

options.A: £0 fixed fee, £5 per instrument, less £3 per complete four
options.B: £3 fixed fee, £5 per instrument, less £3 per complete four
options.C: £3 fixed fee, £5 per instrument, less £2 per complete four
options.D: £3 fixed fee, £4 per instrument, less £3 per complete four
options.E: £3 fixed fee, £6 per instrument, less £3 per complete four

questions.explanation: Every set in the original rule costs £17, with £3 added just once. Four hires at £5 minus a £3 discount also give £17 per complete set.

studyPath.title: Start with technique
steps: Read the official Question Guide. Choose one Critical Thinking type and one Problem Solving type you find difficult.
Do five questions per type without a timer. Before reviewing, write down which rule or step you used.
Explain the correct answer in a sentence and note what made the distractor appealing.

studyPath.title: Add time pressure
steps: Do a Daily 5 and flag correct guesses as well as misses.
Use about 109 seconds per question as a practice benchmark. Finish a short set before checking the answers.
Retry a miss without notes in one or two days, then try an unseen item in the same skill.

studyPath.title: Rehearse all three modules
steps: Complete a Ratio mock and then an unseen Pearson sample, with 40 minutes per module and no calculator or dictionary.
Compare separate raw Critical Thinking and Problem Solving results. Do not average them or convert them to estimated official scaled scores.
Choose one writing prompt and use the studio checklist after completing your draft.
